title: Count retirement-notice occurrences inside merged check-credit text
outcome: Retirement-notice regressions distinguish duplicate notice clauses after check-credit messages merge.
acceptance: Retirement-notice assertions count complete retirement-notice clauses across the entire pending text, including multiple notices merged into one check-credit line, rather than counting lines.

A deterministic regression uses the production pending-line merge to show that two retirement clauses form one line and are counted as two; single-notice, no-notice and unrelated check-credit text controls distinguish the intended clause.

The change is confined to tests; original fingerprint/start checks, consumed-before-terminal repeated-start silence, both actual ACP retirement routes, matching liveness, ordinary-test silence and later-carry refusal remain covered.

Focused validation and an independent Codex/Claude review pair cover the exact input with no outstanding in-scope Medium or higher; Merger owns final combined carry audit, exact full gate and independent acceptance before landing.
